newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cites Italy, Thailand on copyright piracy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cites Italy, Thailand on copyright piracy.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Tuesday about piracy of videos, sound recordings and patents in Italy and Thailand, while it praised Taiwan for efforts taken against copyright theft.

"Taiwan has made a serious effort to address (intellectual property rights) problems over the last six months and has achieved considerable success," said acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in a statement.
But Barshefsky said Italy and Thailand have not done enough to protect copyrights and other intellectual property from theft.

Copyright industries, including computer software, films, television shows, books and music, represent about five percent of U.S. gross domestic product, and their protection is important to the U.S. economy, the trade representative said.

Barshefsky said counterfeiting of videos and sound recordings remained a major problem in Italy, and the government's proposed anti-piracy legislation fails to toughen criminal penalties against copyright theft sufficiently.
"Italy appears to have some of the lowest criminal penalties in Europe and one of the highest rates of piracy," Barshefsky said.

She said it was a "long-festering" problem that needed to be brought under control before the trade representative's office issues a report next April that announces whether action will be taken against countries failing to protect U.S. copyrights.

Barshefsky noted that Thailand enacted legislation that set up intellectual property courts, calling the move a positive development. She said she hoped to see the courts put into operation "as a vehicle for obtaining swift, effective justice" against piracy and counterfeiting.
Still, Thailand remained on the so-called "watch list" for possible trade enforcement action. Barshefsky urged the Thai government to enact legislation to protect patents.
"With continued progress on copyright enforcement, enactment of patent legislation would enable the United States to consider favorably Thailand's removal from the watch list," she said.
The three countries were subject to a special U.S. review on copyright and patent protection.
